title: add RAG agent templates and tool-calling quickstarts; docs site updates
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Added RAG agent templates and multiple tool-calling quickstarts + docs site examples. No breaking changes.
body:
Summary:
This PR introduces a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent templates, three tool-calling quickstarts (Python/TS/Go), and accompanying docs site updates. The goal is to make it easier for engineers to onboard RAG workflows and to demonstrate how to wire agents to external tools (search, DB, ticketing) using the Redwood API and SDKs.

Motivation and context:
- ENG-4821: customers request canonical RAG templates and end-to-end examples for tool calling.
- Provide consistent examples across SDKs and the docs site to reduce support questions and speed developer onboarding.

What this changes (high level):
- New templates: templates/rag/agent_template_basic.yaml, templates/rag/agent_template_chain_of_tools.yaml
- Quickstarts: examples/quickstarts/rag-python-tool-calling, examples/quickstarts/rag-ts-tool-calling, examples/quickstarts/rag-go-tool-calling
- Docs: docs/docs-site/content/guides/rag-agent-quickstart.md (with runnable snippets and links to the examples repo)
- Tests & CI: added lightweight examples smoke tests and example integration checks in .github/workflows/examples.yml

Checklist:
- [x] Add RAG templates and example agent configs
- [x] Implement quickstarts for Python/TS/Go SDKs
- [x] Update docs site with guide and code snippets
- [x] Add CI smoke tests for examples
- [x] Add basic eval prompt set to catch regressions

Commits (summary):
- 4a2f8c2: feat(rag): add base agent template and readme
- b71d9a0: feat(examples): add python quickstart and test harness
- c32e7b1: feat(examples): add typescript quickstart + runnable playground config
- 1f4b9d3: feat(examples): add go quickstart and small helper lib
- d9a2c4f: docs: update docs site guide + examples links
- e5f6b7a: ci: add examples smoke workflow + matrix for SDK versions

Files changed (high level):
- templates/rag/* (2 files)
- examples/quickstarts/rag-python-tool-calling/* (6 files)
- examples/quickstarts/rag-ts-tool-calling/* (6 files)
- examples/quickstarts/rag-go-tool-calling/* (5 files)
- docs/docs-site/content/guides/rag-agent-quickstart.md (1 file)
- .github/workflows/examples.yml (1 file)

Notes on implementation details:
- The agent templates are intentionally small and documented; they show intent-based routing, memory config (KV cache), and an example tool schema for a search API.
- Tool-calling examples demonstrate a minimal and recommended approach: validate tool schemas, use explicit tool calls where appropriate, and provide safe fallbacks to non-tool responses.
- Quickstarts include a small local-storage retrieval example (faiss-lite) so users can run end-to-end without external infra. Each quickstart has a CI smoke test that boots the example, runs a single scripted flow, and asserts expected traces/outputs.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ava Chen: "Nice work. Can we simplify the Python quickstart to avoid additional dependencies?"
  - Samir: "Agree, removed the heavy dependency and replaced with faiss-lite wrapper; updated README to call out optional advanced steps."
- Diego Martinez: "Docs look good; let's ensure the examples are pinned to SDK minor versions so CI is stable."
  - Samir: "Pinned SDK versions in example package files and added matrix in CI."
- Priya Nair: "Add a note on security considerations for tool-calling in the docs (privileged tool access)."
  - Samir: "Added Security section with recommended patterns and KMS mention."

CI and checks:
- .github/workflows/ci: build (pass), unit tests (pass), lint (pass)
- .github/workflows/examples.yml: examples smoke tests (pass on matrix: python 3.10/3.11, node 18, go 1.20)
- Netlify docs preview: generated and links validated

Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking changes to existing runtime or SDK APIs. Templates and quickstarts are additive.

Merge strategy:
- Squash and merge after approvals. Merged by Samir Patel on 2025-02-18.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4902: add end-to-end telemetry examples showing tracing across agent -> tool calls.
- PM-218: capture usage metrics from quickstarts to inform UX improvements.

If you want to run locally:
1) cd examples/quickstarts/rag-python-tool-calling
2) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
3) pip install -r requirements.txt
4) REDWOOD_API_KEY=... make run-local

This PR aims to reduce time-to-first-success for developers integrating RAG + tool-calling on Redwood. Feedback welcome.
